title: Runtime bound for the oracle host simulation
statement: Let $M$ be a Boolean oracle Turing machine and $C$ a Boolean multitape Turing machine with $c>0$ work tapes, and choose states $en,ex$ of $C$. Let $O$ be an oracle language, let $\tau:\mathbb{N}\to\mathbb{N}$, and let $a\in\mathbb{N}$. Assume that for every Boolean word $z$, the machine $C$, started in state $en$ with $z$ on its first work tape and all other tapes blank, reaches after some positive number $t_z\le a(\tau(|z|)+|z|+2)$ of steps the standard configuration in state $ex$ whose first work tape contains the one-symbol answer indicating whether $z\in O$, and does not visit $ex$ earlier. Let $x$ be an input word and let $w$ assign a Boolean word to each of the $k+1$ work tapes of $M$, with the query tape blank. For every $t\in\mathbb{N}$, there is a time $s$ at most $$(2a+13)(t+1)^2+(2a+13)\sum_{r<t}\begin{cases}\tau(|z_r|),&\text{if the oracle computation is in its query state at time }r,\\0,&\text{otherwise},\end{cases}$$ where $z_r$ is the query string at that time, such that the host, started on input $x$ in its initial state with the tape words obtained by extending $w$ with blanks, reaches the stable encoding of the oracle machine's configuration after $t$ steps for some side tag.
